claims.text: 9 out of 10 Gusto customers would recommend Gusto
Gusto customers save an average of 152 hours per year on tax and compliance by switching to Gusto
Gusto has a 4.5/5 star average rating from customers
The 152 hrs/year and 9/10 recommendation statistics are based on a survey of 538 Gusto customers conducted in September 2024
Gusto serves 500,000+ small and medium-sized businesses
Gusto plans start at $49/month plus $6/month per person
A Gusto Meta ad states plans start at $55 a month
Gusto positions itself as 'an all-in-one payroll and HR platform' in its FAQ
Gusto's core payroll product is designed for US-based businesses
Gusto's Canada EOR service is powered by Remote
Gusto offers international contractor payments as an add-on
Gusto runs Meta ads with the copy 'Run payroll, onboard employees, manage time off, handle benefits, and stay compliant, with just one login'
Gusto runs Meta ads targeting S-corp solopreneurs with the Gusto Solo sub-brand
Gusto runs Meta ads featuring Oakland Ballers GM Laura Geist as a customer story
Gusto runs Meta ads with the copy 'As your team grows, Gusto keeps payroll, HR, and benefits simple and scalable'
Gusto launched its Spring 2026 Showcase on April 23, 2026, featuring nearly 75 product updates
Spring 2026 Showcase included a feature called Assisted Payroll Prep, which flags unusual timesheet changes before payroll submission
Spring 2026 Showcase included a Gusto Pro Dashboard aimed at accountants needing compliance visibility across clients
Spring 2026 Showcase included a Benefits Advisor feature for guiding business owners on benefits selection
Spring 2026 Showcase included Gusto 401(k) powered by Guideline, combining payroll and retirement in one dashboard
Spring 2026 Showcase included Time Tracking in the Mobile App for admin approval of timesheets
Spring 2026 Showcase included Automated Contractor Payments
Spring 2026 Showcase included Instant and Same-Day Pay
Gusto surpassed $1 billion in trailing 12-month revenue as announced May 7, 2026
Gusto CEO Josh Reeves stated 'We don't view Gusto as a tool, we aspire to be a partner to small businesses' in the Spring 2026 Showcase press release
Gusto's Head of Product Marketing described an AI/automation feature that can pull data from Google Sheets to calculate bonuses and run payroll
Gusto's AI automation feature was described as coming 'out of the box with ideas on how to automate all the things you already do on Gusto' to avoid the blank canvas problem
Gusto's all-in-one messaging covers payroll, HR, and benefits but does not include IT management, device provisioning, or spend management

Gusto's Gusto Pro Dashboard is framed around accountant/bookkeeper use cases, signaling an accounting channel GTM motion
Gusto Solo is actively advertised via multiple concurrent Meta ads targeting S-corp solopreneurs, indicating a downmarket product investment
Gusto's 401(k) product is a partnership with Guideline, not a natively built capability
